builder: Custom infill build (listed by Maywright Property Co.)
incentives: None advertised: the listing doesn't mention a rate buydown or closing-cost credit. After 11 price cuts and two pulled listings over two years, a seller credit is worth asking for.
ratingWhy: A healthy market with one sick corner: new homes that have sat are being cut hard.
writeup:
Indianapolis isn't a distressed market. Across all sales, prices were up about 1.5% from a year earlier through mid-2026, supply sat at roughly 2.6 months, and builders report strong demand in the master-planned suburbs, helped by buyers moving in from pricier metros.

The pain is narrow but real: new homes that haven't sold. Among the 103 new-construction listings we track there that have been on the market 60+ days, the typical cut from peak is 9.1%, deeper than any state average in our scan, and 41% are down 10% or more. A lot of them look like this one: custom infill homes priced for a buyer who never showed up. This house first listed at $950,000 in October 2024, was pulled and relisted twice, and is now $529,000. That works out to about $166 a square foot for a 3,187 sq ft new build on a street that runs into the Monon Trail. Active listings across the metro were also up about 10% from a year earlier, so sellers have competition.
bottom: For Indianapolis as a whole there's no bottom to call; prices are still edging up. For aged new builds, not yet: this seller has cut four times since August, most recently on Oct 8. Our city-level trend data is only days old, so the next few weeks will tell us whether these cuts are slowing.
